newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sees steady US rates, stronger yen.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sees steady US rates, stronger yen.

text.p: Chrysler Corp chief economist Van Bussmann said he believes the Federal Reserve Board will leave interest rates unchanged in November and added that he expects the yen to strengthen against the dollar next year.

In a conference call with reporters following the release of Chrysler's third quarter earnings, Bussmann said he believes that the Fed's governors recognize that there is little inflationary pressure in the U.S. economy.

"I don't think they're going to raise rates when they meet in November," he said, referring to policy makers who serve on the Fed's Federal Open Market Committee. "They perceive, I think that the economy is growing at a pace that is not going to raise inflation in the future."
He said the natural exchange rate for the yen is about 100 to the dollar. The dollar closed U.S. trading Monday at 111.60/65 yen.

"We think the dollar's likely to be abnormally strong for the next several months," Bussmann said. "But eventually, probably some time in 1997, that situation will reverse and the natural tendency of the yen to strengthen against the dollar -- because of lower inflation and higher productivity growth in Japan than in the U.S. -- will take over and we'll see the dollar start to head down toward and past 100 yen."

Chrysler's top executives have said repeatedly in recent months that the dollar's strength versus the yen gives Japanese automakers a pricing advantage. Several Japanese automakers have introduced new vehicles for the 1997 model year that are priced the same as or below models they replace.
